pr_title: Reduce startup allocation from event pipe metadata
pr_body:
A "hello world" console app results in EventPipeMetadataGenerate.GenerateEventMetadata making almost 500 calls to factory methods on ScalarTypeInfo, each of which allocates a new ScalarTypeInfo object and a Func delegate, but they're all immutable objects that could be cached on first use and reused for all subsequent use.  Eliminating the need for the funcs entirely and caching the ScalarTypeInfo objects saves almost 1000 object allocations and 66K of allocation at startup.  It does mean we'll end up holding on to a few objects (9 objects == ~575 bytes) for the duration of the app that we would otherwise have dropped, plus the various static fields... if you think I should cull this back at all, or that the tradeoff is entirely bad, let me know (other areas of the infrastructure are already doing such caching, mostly implicitly via the compiler's caching of lambdas).

Before:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2642209/110349122-5f2be680-8000-11eb-9638-89ffe56a3bd0.png)

After:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2642209/110349072-50ddca80-8000-11eb-9afa-cefd652da963.png)

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/49285

issue_context.title: Hundreds of ScalarTypeInfo objects being created at startup
issue_context.body:
Hundreds of ScalarTypeInfo objects are being created at startup for a template "hello world" app:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2642209/110270694-5dc4d480-7f94-11eb-85ec-1e0cff0c742e.png)
The allocations stem from:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2642209/110270578-222a0a80-7f94-11eb-9b48-50750a39c9a2.png)
and along with them hundreds of Func delegates.  Almost all of these are for UInt32(), UInt16(), and UInt64(), stemming from these helpers:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7ab65423373f04998f3d365d564b3fc0e55fdf2b/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Diagnostics/Tracing/TraceLogging/SimpleTypeInfos.cs#L73-L87
At quick glance, it appears these are all immutable objects.  Is there any reason these couldn't be singletons?
